failure_mode: PostgreSQL dynamic shared memory /dev/shm exhausted at 8 workers

answers.1_10K_to_100K_exact_latency: Observed 100K p50 156.12 ms versus 10K p50 167.18 ms (0.93×); this is not directly comparable.
answers.2_is_scaling_linear: No linear conclusion is supported: the observed ratio was not near 10× and the load/projection protocols and runtime state differ.
answers.3_dominant_time_component: Exact vector scan/sort plus service candidate hydration dominates the service path; representative plans are preserved.
answers.4_metadata_filter_workload_reduction: The 10% treatment reduced eligible candidates from 100,000 to 10,000 (90%); 1% and 50% treatments behaved consistently.
answers.5_temporal_extra_cost: Current-fact temporal SQL p50 was 301.25 ms versus exact service p50 156.12 ms; paths differ, so this is not a pure overhead ratio.
answers.6_planner_behavior: Observed plan node types: Bitmap Heap Scan, Bitmap Index Scan, Gather Merge, Hash, Hash Join, Index Scan, Limit, Nested Loop, Seq Scan, Sort; no ANN index existed.
answers.7_bulk_vs_incremental: COPY achieved 20279.41 rows/s while single-request service ingest achieved 57.49 memories/s; protocols are intentionally not equated.
answers.8_concurrency_first_saturation: Dynamic shared memory (/dev/shm), not the database volume, saturated first at 8 workers; 44/64 operations failed and the experiment stopped.
answers.9_memory_footprint: Final run schema size was 167550976 bytes (1675.5 bytes per main memory including schema/fixture overhead) for 96-d vectors.
answers.10_current_largest_bottleneck: At single-query load the dominant path is exact vector scan/sort and service hydration; under concurrency the hard bottleneck was the container's 64 MiB dynamic shared-memory mount.

evidence_level: executed A-F; failed G; H not executed by stop condition
what_this_proves: observed exact, filter, temporal, ingest, delete and concurrency saturation behavior
